solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pass on from Sunak — falling short after record in recession

indicators.note: something falling short does not reach its end, so the final letter is lost
a recession is a going backwards, so the letters run back to front

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Rishi Sunak, former UK prime minister

explanation.surface: A political commentator passes on a remark from the former prime minister about a disappointing record during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was UK prime minister 2022-24, so Sunak stands for his first name. The record goes in front even though 'after' comes later in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a gentle euphemism for dying, which is exactly what perishing means.

clue.text: Beat poet’s debut at posh educational establishment

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'
the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A Beat poet makes a first appearance at an elite university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat poet' suggests the Beat Generation, but 'Beat' is the definition on its own. U is the old label for upper-class usage; the LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the rhythmic throb of the heart, a regular beat felt at the wrist.

clue.text: Straps controlling movement on either side of mum’s stays

indicators.note: a piece sitting on both sides of another wraps around it

blocks.note: reins are straps used to steer a horse
Ma is a familiar word for mother; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: Harness straps fitted around a mother's corset stays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' reads as corset bones in the surface, but it is a plural noun for what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains and stays are both plural nouns for leftovers or relics, in the sense of what is still left behind.

clue.text: Owing nothing and single in the beginning

indicators.note: the word joins two pieces, so they simply sit one after the other

blocks.note: being all square means no debts are outstanding
single means one

explanation.surface: Starting out debt-free and unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a fresh start in life; the definition is the starting point itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to square one means returning to the very start, as on a board game's first space.

clue.text: Go on earliest of teach-ins with spiritual leader

indicators.note: earliest points to what comes first, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A religious leader drones on at the start of some teaching sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' lets the rabbi come first. 'Rabbit on' is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit (on) is to talk at tedious length, the same as going on.

clue.text: Help getting Virginia into trouble

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, as something goes into a box

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone seeks assistance after Virginia lands in a difficult situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to ail.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or be of use, as in 'it will avail you nothing'.

clue.text: Throw up on interminably relentless supporter

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
without an end, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

blocks.note: to lob is to throw high
stern means harsh and unyielding

explanation.surface: A fan of a team being sick over a merciless supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as vomiting, but the two words are separate jobs: throw is the word and up flips it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolster is a long pillow that props someone up, so it is literally a supporter.

clue.text: Said oddly after article looking into Alexander-Arnold’s passing

indicators.note: oddly picks out the letters in odd-numbered places
one piece follows the other in sequence
something looking into a place has its head inside it

blocks.note: Trent Alexander-Arnold, the England footballer
the indefinite article
the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece examines a footballer's passing game, with some odd quotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like football skill but means fleeting. Alexander-Arnold is the Liverpool and England defender whose first name is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient lasts only a short time, just as a passing mood soon fades away.

clue.text: Uproar, caused by strike in sovereign’s household, cut short

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
trimming the end off removes the last letter

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or strike
a monarch's court is the royal household

explanation.surface: A scandal at the palace after a royal staff walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is the old verb meaning to thrash. The royal household is shortened before it takes the strike inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud, insistent public outcry, a close synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Letter describing murder victim reportedly in motionless representation of historical scene

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw round, so one piece encircles another
what is reported is heard rather than seen, so go by sound

blocks.note: tau is a Greek letter
Abel was killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A letter detailing a killing appears in a staged historical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence but is a Greek letter. Abel, the first murder victim in Genesis, sounds like ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a scene posed silently by actors who stay still, like a living picture.

clue.text: Make operative do something that’s involving tax on sulphur

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up, so one piece holds another
in a down clue the piece sitting on another comes directly above it

blocks.note: to act is to do something
i.e., id est, means 'that is'
value added tax
chemical symbol

explanation.surface: An instruction to an agent to take action over a tax on sulphur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operative' suggests a secret agent, but 'Make operative' is the definition. 'That's' hides the Latin abbreviation for 'that is', which wraps the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate something is to set it working, which means making it operative or functional.

clue.text: Given in return for beaten-up police car without a hint of rust

indicators.note: something beaten up is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
in its old sense without means outside, so these letters go round another
a hint is just a small first trace, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something offered in exchange for a battered but rust-free patrol car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: the rearranged letters sit outside the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Reciprocal describes something given or done in return, as a mutual exchange between two parties.

clue.text: Nick almost admitting son’s a piece of work

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
to admit is to let in, so one piece takes another inside

blocks.note: to nick is to take or steal
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A boy called Nick almost confesses that his son is a nasty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of work' sounds like an insult about the son, but here it is literal: a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a job to be done, literally a piece of work assigned to someone.

clue.text: Attempt to capture American tenor’s zest

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside

blocks.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
abbreviation for the United States
T is the first letter of tenor, its usual abbreviation in music; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: An effort to record a US singer's enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' suggests a singer; here it is just the abbreviation T, added after US inside GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and energy, the same lively relish that zest describes.

clue.text: Earnest fellow flipped over date’s unappealing shift

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so its letters run backwards
in a down entry one piece placed over another simply comes before it

blocks.note: grave means serious
Ray is a man's name, standing for any chap
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A serious man goes head over heels over a romantic partner's dull job rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' looks like a romantic partner but is just D. The definition needs the whole of 'unappealing shift'.
explanation.definitionFit: The graveyard shift is the night work rota, after midnight, which few people want to work.

clue.text: Learned when playing well at Leeds regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: a player in form is playing well
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A footballer learns what it is like to play well at Leeds United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like a past-tense verb, but it is the adjective meaning well-read.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person is knowledgeable and well-read, so informed is a close adjectival synonym here.

clue.text: Trump up for broadcast after ABC conceals investigator’s source

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are mixed up
concealing something means hiding it inside
a source is where something starts, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A news network hides an investigative journalist's informant in a story about Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' wants to be the former US president, but 'Trump up' is the definition. 'After' is not a placement word here: it is part of the letters shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump up a charge is to invent it falsely, which is what fabricating evidence means.

clue.text: Dance hall’s opening a long time after prohibition

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so the first letter is used
one piece follows another in sequence

blocks.note: first letter of the word
taken as written
a ban prohibits
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A dance hall finally opens its doors long after Prohibition ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance hall' looks like one phrase, but 'Dance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance in duple time, famous from the aria in Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Party devotee dismissing head of policy as a crafty type

indicators.note: dismissing the head removes the front letter

blocks.note: a partisan is a committed supporter of a party
its head is its first letter, which is the one dismissed

explanation.surface: A loyal party member ignores the policy chief, seeing them as sly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' suggests cunning, but here it is literal: someone skilled at a craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things, someone who works at a craft.

clue.text: Explosion of plant disease

blocks.note: first meaning: a violent burst or detonation
second meaning: a fungal disease that withers crops such as rice

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sudden outbreak of disease; the two halves are separate meanings joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a violent detonation and a fungal blight that shrivels the flowers or grain of cereal crops.

clue.text: Not confined in an area aimed at mostly around lake

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
going around something encloses it

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
what is aimed at is a target
L for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: An escaped animal is roaming freely somewhere near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: TARGET loses its last letter and wraps L after its T; A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped prisoner or animal at large is free and uncaptured, so not confined anywhere.

clue.text: Discharge coming? Not today

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to leave something out

blocks.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
AD, Anno Domini, labels the present era

explanation.surface: A worried question about an expected release, answered with a promise of delay.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (Anno Domini) marks the era we live in, so it stands for today; removing it from ADVENT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To vent is to let out or release, as steam escapes or as anger is expressed.

clue.text: Expert, 51, featured in escapist novel

indicators.note: what is featured in something appears inside it
novel means new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable 51-year-old appears in a fantasy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal. The number 51 becomes Roman LI.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist has deep knowledge of one field, making them an authority on that subject.

clue.text: Rock climbers finally getting acclaim in speech

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the last letter is used
in speech means as heard, so go by the sound
one piece receives the next, which follows it

blocks.note: last letter of the word
to hail is to acclaim

explanation.surface: Mountaineers are praised in speeches after scaling a crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock climbers' reads as one phrase, but 'Rock' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale is a soft, layered sedimentary stone formed from compacted mud and clay.

clue.text: View of soldiers heading north near the outskirts of Hobart

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters are kept
one piece sits right next to the other

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Troops marching north catch a glimpse of the edge of the Tasmanian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobart is the capital of Tasmania, in Australia; only its outer letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something seen, a vista or scene, so it can stand in for a view.

clue.text: Arrange in order to hit back at quiet gangster

indicators.note: going back means reading in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to ram is to hit hard
the call for silence
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Planning a counterattack against a silent mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order to' looks like a phrase meaning 'so as to', but 'in order' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops or facts is to put them into proper ranks or sequence.

clue.text: Hotchpotch of rules embraced by football bosses in the past

indicators.note: what is embraced is held in the arms, so it sits inside

blocks.note: the Football Association runs English football
R is an abbreviation for rule, doubled for the plural
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Football's governing body once adopted a muddled set of regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Football Association runs the game in England, so its initials stand for football bosses. Only those initials do the embracing; the past simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble of things, much like a hotchpotch or mixture.

clue.text: Risk of death at the start fisherman left out

indicators.note: the start is the first letter only
left out means omitted, so a letter for the word left goes

blocks.note: first letter of the word
an angler fishes with rod and line
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An angler stranded at the start of a trip faces mortal peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as stranded, but 'left' is L and 'out' says remove it from ANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger is exposure to possible harm, the same threat of injury that risk describes.

clue.text: Single out line maintained by witness at court

indicators.note: something maintained is held up by what surrounds it
one piece is next to the other

blocks.note: L for line
to witness is to see
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A witness in court is asked to pick out a suspect from a line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witness' looks like a person in court but is the verb see.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to choose one particular item from a group, which is what singling out means.
